summary: A screenshot beautifier as one static page: drop, paste or pick a screenshot, adjust padding, corners, shadow, background and canvas ratio with live preview, export a crisp PNG at 1x or 2x or copy it to the clipboard. Everything happens in the browser; nothing is uploaded; it works offline after the first load.

stack.choice: One HTML file, vanilla JS, Canvas 2D
stack.why: no framework, no build step, no server, no dependency to break

stack.choice: Any static host, or open the file

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: A Chromium browser and Safari
prerequisites.why: Clipboard image copying behaves differently in Safari; Phase 5 must be tested in both.
prerequisites.get: Chrome or Edge, plus Safari if you have a Mac. Without Safari, note the clipboard code path is untested there.

prerequisites.name: A few screenshots to test with
prerequisites.why: Including one very tall one and one wider than 4000px, to exercise ratios and performance.
prerequisites.get: Take three: a normal window, a full-page tall capture, a large retina one.

prerequisites.name: A static host (optional)
prerequisites.why: To share it with others. Locally, opening the file is enough.
prerequisites.get: Cloudflare Pages, Netlify or GitHub Pages: connect the repo, done.

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

phases.title: Image input and render loop
phases.goal: Three ways in, one render function, correct on HiDPI from the start.

steps.do: Create index.html with a canvas, a sidebar and one state object
steps.detail: state = { image, padding, radius, shadow, background, ratio, scale }. Every control writes to state and calls render(). Exactly one render function; two code paths drawing to the canvas is the classic bug here.

steps.do: Wire drag-and-drop, paste and a file picker
steps.detail: paste: read clipboardData.items for an image type. All three create an Image from a Blob URL and set state.image.
Backing store = css size times devicePixelRatio; ctx.scale once. Retrofitting this later means re-tuning every offset.

check: All three input paths load the same image identically
The render is crisp on a HiDPI display
A 5000px-wide screenshot loads without freezing the page

phases.title: Geometry controls
phases.goal: Padding, radius and shadow as live sliders whose export matches the preview.

steps.detail: Range inputs bound to state; render on input.

steps.do: Clip rounded corners with a real path
steps.detail: ctx.roundRect and clip, not a CSS overlay, or the export will not match the preview. Draw the shadow with canvas shadow properties on the clipped shape.

check: Every slider updates the preview within one frame
Corners are genuinely transparent at the edges
The shadow follows the rounded shape, not the bounding box

phases.title: Backgrounds
phases.goal: Ten presets that look premium before anyone touches anything.

steps.do: Add a preset picker with gradients, multi-stop meshes and solids
steps.detail: Plus a custom colour input and a transparent option.

steps.do: Make the default the best one

check: Every preset renders correctly at every ratio
The transparent option exports a PNG with a real alpha channel

phases.title: Canvas ratios

steps.do: Add the ratio selector: original, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1 and 2:1
steps.detail: Store it in state; a change triggers one render().

steps.do: Fit the image inside the padding without cropping and centre it on both axes
steps.detail: Compute the scale as the minimum of available width over image width and available height over image height. Never crop, never distort.

check: Switching ratios never crops the screenshot
A very tall screenshot fits inside a 16:9 canvas

phases.title: Export
phases.goal: Sharp PNG at 1x and 2x, and clipboard that works in both engines.

steps.do: Export by rendering to an offscreen canvas at the target scale
Copy to clipboard the portable way
steps.detail: Pass a Promise resolving to a Blob into ClipboardItem; Safari requires the promise form and Chromium accepts it. Call navigator.clipboard.write synchronously inside the click handler.

check: The 2x export is exactly twice the pixels and visibly sharper
The exported file matches the preview pixel for pixel in layout
Paste works in both Safari and a Chromium browser

phases.title: Polish
phases.goal: Shortcuts, an empty state, memory, offline.

steps.do: Add keyboard shortcuts, reset, and remembered settings in localStorage wrapped in try/catch
Write the empty state and a visible nothing-is-uploaded note
Confirm offline: no external requests at all
steps.detail: Open DevTools > Network, reload with Offline checked.

check: The page works with the network disabled
A first-time user knows what to do without instructions

phases.title: Ship it as an app
phases.goal: Only for the product path: installable, offline-first, with a privacy statement.

steps.do: Add a web app manifest and a service worker that caches the one file
Deploy to a static host with a custom domain and a one-line privacy note
steps.detail: Nothing is uploaded; there is no analytics.

check: The site installs as an app and opens offline
The deployed page makes zero network requests after first load

product.outcome: An installable, offline screenshot tool with a defensible privacy statement: the code is the policy.

architecture.owns: the single state object and render()
architecture.swap: The whole app is this; keep it one file
Add a share-target in the manifest later
Add WebP or JPEG output here only

operations.backup: The repo is the backup. There is no state anywhere else.
operations.monitoring: An uptime check on the URL. Nothing else can fail.
operations.incident: A broken deploy is reverted with git; there is no data to lose.

releaseGate: Zero network requests after first load
Clipboard copy verified in Safari and Chromium

notIncluded: A template and device-frame library. Keeping frames current is real ongoing work and a real reason to pay.
Batch processing and automatic text redaction.
Cloud sync of presets. There is no cloud here.
after: Device frames as SVG overlays you maintain yourself
A share-target so phones can send screenshots straight in
